message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.34","text":"Oh, the great hand of the wise God, which makes all things in all things! For a countless multitude of birds has been brought into being by him, and this multitude is diverse, each bird differing from another in every respect—I mean their colors, beaks, claws, eyes, dispositions, voices, and all the other features. And how many different forms of plants there are, distinguished by countless colors, qualities, and scents! And how many animals there are on dry land and in the waters! It is impossible to tell of their shapes, forms, locations, colors, ways of life, dispositions, natures, and multitude, and further of the multitudes and heights of mountains, the differences among stones, fearsome recesses, springs, rivers, lakes, seas, harbors, islands, forests, the whole inhabited world, and uninhabited places.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς μεγάλης θεοῦ φρονίμου χειρός","chosen":"the great hand of the wise God","rationale":"Because φρόνιμος is a two-termination adjective, φρονίμου can qualify either θεοῦ or χειρός. The main text attaches it to the immediately preceding θεοῦ, yielding “the great hand of the wise God.” Alternatively, attaching it to χειρός gives “the great, wise hand of God,” an interpretation supported by the following description of the hand’s activity."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐν πᾶσιν πάντα ποιούσης","chosen":"which makes all things in all things","rationale":"The rendering preserves the repeated πᾶς wording and its broad scope. “Which does everything in every sphere” is a possible interpretive alternative."},{"source_quote":"καὶ οὗτος ποικίλος, πρὸς τὸν ἕτερον κατὰ πάντα ἐξηλλαγμένος","chosen":"and this multitude is diverse, each bird differing from another in every respect","rationale":"The collective noun ὄχλος is masculine singular, and οὗτος and ἐξηλλαγμένος agree with it grammatically. The main rendering understands the comparison distributively among the birds because the following catalogue names their distinguishing features. Alternatively, the phrase may compare one collective group or kind of birds with another: “and this multitude is diverse, differing in every respect from the other group or kind.”"},{"source_quote":"βλέμματα, γνώμας, φθέγματα","chosen":"eyes, dispositions, voices","rationale":"βλέμματα can mean looks, gazes, or eyes; γνώμαι denotes dispositions or traits of mind; φθέγματα denotes uttered sounds or voices."},{"source_quote":"θέσεις","chosen":"locations","rationale":"θέσις literally denotes placement or position. In this catalogue of animal differences, “locations” is cautious; “habitats” or “postures” are possible contextual alternatives."},{"source_quote":"ὀρέων πλήθη καὶ ὕψη","chosen":"the multitudes and heights of mountains","rationale":"The plural πλήθη denotes the quantity or numerousness of the mountains. “The numbers and heights of mountains” is a less formal alternative."},{"source_quote":"μυχοὺς φοβερούς","chosen":"fearsome recesses","rationale":"μυχός denotes an inner recess or depth. “Fearsome depths” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ὕλας","chosen":"forests","rationale":"Although ὕλη can mean matter or material, the geographical catalogue supports its concrete sense “woods” or “forests.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"πόσα δὲ τῆς χέρσου ζῷα καὶ τῶν ἐν ὕδασιν, ὧν ἀδύνατον, εἰπεῖν σχήματα, μορφάς, θέσεις, χρώματα, βίους, γνώμας, φύσεις, ὄχλον. ἔτι τε ὀρέων πλήθη καὶ ὕψη, λίθων διαφοράς, μυχοὺς φοβερούς, πηγάς, ποταμούς, λίμνας, θαλάσσας, λιμένας, νήσους, ὕλας, οἰκουμένην τε πᾶσαν καὶ ἀοικήτους τόπους.","issue":"The edition prints a full stop after ὄχλον, but the following catalogue contains explicitly accusative items, beginning with διαφοράς, that naturally continue or elliptically resume as objects of εἰπεῖν. The main translation therefore keeps the ensuing catalogue within the scope of “it is impossible to tell of.” Alternatively, the printed punctuation may be represented by an elliptical new catalogue: “And further: the multitudes and heights of mountains...” This is an interpretive question concerning the surviving syntax and editorial punctuation, not a missing or unreadable text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
